analysis.title: International Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing (October 14, 2026)
key_insights: Tentative signs of market broadening faded on Oct 13, with tech weakness the main theme. ASML's Q3 print looks light on information, and JPM's EU tech specialist expects disappointment over the lack of incremental detail on 2027 guidance and 2028 capacity.

Global rates found some respite, helped by dovish Fed speak, despite rising oil (overnight escalation in the Middle East and Russia/Ukraine, rising shipping costs). US and EU futures point to a modestly higher open.
China PPI rose 1.1% m/m seasonally adjusted, much faster than consumer goods prices. JPM reads this as weak end-demand constraining pass-through and squeezing margins.
China is nearing a $1tn trade surplus as exports surge, and is set to exceed 2025's record. It also reported a record $35bn trade surplus with the EU.

Last week's EU/China trade talks lowered near-term disruption risks and created a more structured process for managing disputes, but did not resolve the trade imbalance. The clearest result was on EVs. European leaders assess the outcome in a 2-day meeting starting tomorrow. JPM Econ's 3-6 month base case is managed de-escalation alongside selective pressure.

EU and US banks de-rated through September. Positioning Intelligence shows hedge funds bought US Banks for a 2nd straight week (+2z), leaning into a potential 4Q rebound, and kept buying the dip in EU banks, though long-term positioning there remains elevated.

Bank earnings are off to a mixed start. JPM's US Banks specialist says investor frustration is increasingly about valuation rather than earnings, and attributes the implied derating to management teams being clearly more cautious than the numbers.
Kian reconfirmed an Overweight on EU banks, with relatively high confidence in their earnings trajectory.
JPM Econ forecasts September US CPI at +0.55% m/m headline (3.6% y/y) and +0.18% m/m core (2.4% y/y). Global inflation momentum is turning higher again on broad-based goods price pressures.

China A-shares: domestic liquidity remains subdued, with velocity, margin financing and ETF flows low and no sign yet of meaningful funding from central government-backed institutions. JPM favors a barbell of high yielders (defensive) and AI plus CXO/innovative drugs (growth). Memory and Server/switch ODM/OEM have reasonable valuations. A meaningful upward revision to the AI capex target would be a clear positive.
EU natural gas: weekly demand picked up on colder weather. October is seen in line with or slightly above the 10-year normal. Preliminary September demand averaged 330 Mcm/day, about 10% lower y/y.

Market Intelligence is tactically bullish on global equities. Regional preference is long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus EU, because the US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation and Asia has pockets of both.

Broadening can return, more clearly in the US than the EU. European earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but EGB spreads need to stabilize before broadening gains conviction in the EU.

EM monetization: EM has recovered over 9% of its drawdown since the end-July bottom but remains below YTD highs. JPM is bullish EM on global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds, commodity-driven broadening and room for policy easing. It expects country and sector divergence and prefers country-relative trades.

Positioning Intelligence weekly wrap: HF performance is -0.8% MTD in October. Equity L/S is the laggard (-1.2% globally), and EU managers are hit hardest (-1.3% MTD) with EU Banks a notable detractor.

HF flows were lackluster (turnover ~0.5z below average). US net flows increasingly correlate with market direction, which suggests HFs could amplify moves. Retail flows and sentiment remain low while ETF flows are rebounding.
EU vs US positioning gap is stretched: US positioning is steady (TPM ~46th percentile) while Europe saw -1.7z net selling this week and sits near the 13th percentile.

Semis were the most net sold industry by HFs in North America (-1.5z) and EMEA (-3z), with only AxJ buying (+1z). They remain a top-2 net exposure industry in every region. Utilities are near historically low HF positioning even as ETF flows turned positive. Biotech remains weak but paused de-grossing.

vol_and_positioning: HF performance is -0.8% MTD in October. Equity L/S is -1.2% globally and EU managers are -1.3% MTD. Quants are ~flat MTD.
HFs bought US Banks for a 2nd straight week (just over +2z). Large caps were bought (+1.5z over 5 days, positioning near highs) and regionals sold (-0.9z, low 12m positioning).
EU Banks were modestly bought by HFs (<+1z), but positioning is elevated (+3z vs LT).
EU net selling was -1.7z this week, with aggregate EU positioning at ~13th percentile versus US TPM at ~46th percentile.
Semis were net sold: -1.5z in N. America and -3z in EMEA, with AxJ buying +1z.
HF turnover ~0.5z below average. Net flows in the US are increasingly correlated with market moves, which suggests HFs could amplify direction.
Option hedges: keep MCX < UKX until clarity emerges on spending, pragmatism and ideology, and short FR vs EU Domestics on politics and dislocation.
geopolitical: Overnight escalation in the Middle East and Russia/Ukraine, with rising shipping costs, pushed oil higher.
